title: Cosine schedule accelerates overfitting on CIFAR-10
description: Models trained with the cosine noise schedule reached optimal performance and then overfitted more quickly than those trained with the linear schedule.
canonical_description: Cosine noise schedule leads to faster overfitting compared to linear schedule

evidence.anchor: cosine schedule tended to reach optimal performance
evidence.quote: Holding dropout constant, we found that models trained with our cosine schedule tended to reach optimal performance (and then overfit) more quickly than those trained with the linear schedule (Figure [REF:fig:overfitting]).

verdict.reasoning: No candidate papers were deep-read, so there is no evidence the gap has been addressed.

ranking.feasibility_reasoning: The gap is highly tractable. CIFAR-10 is freely available and training diffusion models on it is feasible on a single GPU within hours/days — no frontier-scale compute needed. The phenomenon (cosine vs linear noise schedule → different overfitting behavior) is clearly defined and reproducible, so the first step is straightforward. Methodologically, there are mature tools for analyzing training dynamics, loss landscapes, and memorization in diffusion models (e.g., noise-distribution analysis, gradient dot-product metrics, effective data dimensionality). The scope is focused: explain a specific empirical difference between two schedules. Evaluability is clear — overfitting can be measured via train/test FID gap or loss divergence. The main challenge is isolating the causal mechanism among plausible candidates (e.g., different exposure to high-noise steps, altered signal-to-noise ratio trajectories, implicit regularization effects), which requires careful controlled experiments but no fundamental breakthrough. Score 0.85 rather than 1.0 because the mechanism is not yet obvious, so some exploratory work is needed to narrow down hypotheses.
